newsitem.title: DUBAI: UAE market slow, investors await news on two firms.
newsitem.headline: UAE market slow, investors await news on two firms.

text.p: Trade was slow on the unofficial United Arab Emirates stock market in the week to Thursday, with investors waiting for news on two new companies, brokers said.
The National Bank of Abu Dhabi (NBAD) index fell 6.94 points to 2,566.58 points in the week. Of the 27 traded companies, the shares of only two rose, seven dropped and the rest were flat.

Brokers said the market was stagnant as investors waited for news on the setting up of two new companies, Abu Dhabi Islamic Bank and Oasis International Leasing Co. The UAE government recently announced their formation.
Shares in the new Emaar Properties slipped in the week to 17 dirhams from 22. But the closing price was still higher than the share's par value of 10 dirhams.

Among the main losers were al-Khazna Insurance, which lost 15 dirhams to 275, and Abu Dhabi Commercial Bank and Union National Bank which fell five dirhams each to close at 350 and 360 dirhams respectively.
